title: agentic.config
description: How a repository works for an agent. `.ai/agentic.config.json` is committed; `.ai/agentic.config.local.json` overrides it on one machine and may tighten `guardrails` and `pr.merge` but never loosen them. A key neither file sets is inferred: the Node package manager from the lockfile, the `conventional` commit preset, and `gate.command` from the manifest's `check` script. Unknown top-level keys are tolerated so other tool families can share the file; the keys named here refuse unknown children.

baseBranch.description: The branch pull requests target; `auto` reads the remote's default branch.

node.description: Inferred from the lockfile. The package-manager guard refuses the other Node package managers only when this is `pnpm`.

ruby.description: Accepted so a repository can declare it; no guard reads it and nothing infers it.

guardrails.description: Policy the local override may tighten and never loosen. Every enum lists its strictest value first.

forcePush.description: `deny` refuses every force push. `lease` lets `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes` through to a branch outside `protectedBranches`; bare `--force` and `-f` stay refused. `ask` is `lease` with a permission prompt for each lease push it lets through. Strictest first: deny, ask, lease.

commitOnProtected.description: `deny` refuses a `git commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick` or `revert` on a branch listed in `protectedBranches`, so every change starts on a branch of its own. `allow` lets it through, for a repository that commits small fixes on its protected branch and pushes them from a person's terminal. Default `allow`. Strictest first: deny, allow.

filteredOutput.description: `deny` refuses a check command whose output a pipe feeds to `head`, `tail`, `grep`, `egrep`, `fgrep`, `rg`, `sed`, `awk`, `less` or `more`: the pipe hides the failure and, with `pipefail` off, the exit code. A check command is the `gate.command`, a Step, a `gate.checks.run` command, `dw-sdlc gate`, `dw-sdlc check`, or a common runner such as `vitest`, `tsc` or `rspec`. `tee` and a redirect pass. `allow` turns the guard off, for a repository whose workflow pipes check output. Default `deny`.

envFiles.description: Which env files (`.env`, `.env.*`, `.envrc`) an agent may read, edit or write. A candidate is judged in this order: listed in `deny` → refused; listed in `allow` → readable; `policy` `deny` → refused; `policy` `git` → readable when git tracks it, refused when git ignores it or does not know it. Entries are globs against the path relative to the repository root: `*` and `?` as in a shell pattern (`*` crosses `/`), a leading `**/` means at any depth, so `.env` is the one in the root and `**/.env.example` every file of that name. No brace groups. A path outside the repository root, or outside any repository, is judged by its basename against the `**/` entries alone. Defaults: policy `git`, allow the `.env.example`, `.env.sample` and `.env.template` names anywhere, deny nothing. The local override may drop `allow` entries and add `deny` entries, never the reverse.

policy.description: What decides a candidate no list names. `deny` refuses it; `git` asks git: tracked passes, ignored or unknown is refused.

allow.description: Globs of the env files that are readable regardless of `policy`.

deny.description: Globs of the env files that are refused regardless of `policy`; wins over `allow`.

protectedBranches.description: Branches the guards refuse every push to: plain, lease or force. Under `commitOnProtected: deny` they refuse a commit, merge, cherry-pick or revert on one too. The local override may add to this list, never remove from it.

convention.description: The subject preset `pattern` falls back to. `ticket-key`: `[KEY-123] type: subject`, the tracker's key in brackets before a type from a fixed list. `conventional`: Conventional Commits; inferred when no layer sets either.

pattern.description: POSIX ERE the commit subject must match; set, it wins over `convention`. `grep -E` runs it, so no `\d`, `\s`, `\w`, `\b` or `(?…)`. `.+` accepts any subject.

trailer.description: A trailer key, such as `Co-Authored-By`, that every commit message must carry on a line of its own.

gate.description: The Gate `dw-sdlc gate` runs: the Steps under `steps` in order, then every Check under `checks`.

command.description: The one command that runs the Gate, the same in a terminal and in CI. Inferred as `pnpm check` where `package.json` has a `check` script.

steps.description: The Steps: toolchain commands run in order from the repository root through `sh -c`; the first that does not pass ends the Gate and no Check runs. A Step is a command string, or an object with its `command` and a `hint`. Each one's output is captured, and its last 50 lines are printed when it does not pass, with the `hint` under them; `--verbose` passes the output through instead. A command the shell cannot find (exit 127) or execute (126) means the Gate cannot run.

hint.description: What to try when the Step fails: one line the Gate prints as `hint: <text>` under the failure. A passing Step prints nothing.

drift.description: Whether a Step may write the tree. `fail`, the default, watches every Step for Drift: before and after each Step the Gate records the content of every file git tracks or would track, and each file the Step created, changed or deleted is one failure, `"<step>" created it`, `changed it` or `deleted it`, without stopping the Steps after it. Ignored files and edits made before the run never drift. A tree the Gate cannot record, outside a git checkout, means the Gate cannot run. `allow` turns the watch off.

checks.description: The Checks the Gate runs after its steps, every one even when another fails: the `run` scripts first, then the Checks the package ships, in the order listed here. A Check the package ships is `true` for its defaults, an options object over them, or `false` to stay off. A key names a Check the package ships, and a name it does not ship is refused.

run.description: The repository's own scripts, each run like a Step and reported as a Check under its `name`: exit 0 passes, 127 or 126 means the Gate cannot run, any other code fails.

name.description: The Check's name, which each of its failure lines carries: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

hint.description: What to try when the script fails: one line the Gate prints as `hint: <text>` under the failure. A passing script prints nothing.

primitives.description: The Primitives catalogue: unique ids, each in a group `groups` lists, a summary of one line within 120 characters, every `code` path on disk, every `docs` path on disk with its heading anchor resolving, and every file under `roots` named by the `code` of a Primitive, itself or a directory above it. A test file, under a `test`, `tests` or `__tests__` directory or named `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*`, needs no Primitive.

file.description: The catalogue, relative to the repository root. Default `.ai/primitives.json`.

roots.description: The directories whose every file a Primitive names, relative to the repository root; one that does not exist names no file. Default `packages`, `plugins`, `scripts` and `src`.

agents-map.description: The agent map: within its byte budget, naming the resolved `gate.command`, carrying a Task Router row to the Primitives catalogue where there is one, every path the Task Router points at existing, `CLAUDE.md` a symbolic link to the map unless the map is `CLAUDE.md`, and the skills directory, `skills-lock.json` and the `.claude/skills` links in step where the repository has them.

file.description: The map, relative to the repository root. Default `AGENTS.md`.

maxBytes.description: The map's budget in bytes. Default 10240.

routed-docs.description: Every document a task leads to: each file `files` matches and `exempt` does not is reached by a Task Router row of the agent map, through a code span in a cell after the first naming it, a directory above it or a glob that matches it, or by the `docs` of a Primitive in the catalogue naming it, its heading anchor dropped; a path reads from the root, `./` or `/` before it or not. The map is the file `agents-map` reads and the catalogue the one `primitives` reads, each Check on or off; a catalogue that is missing or invalid reaches nothing. A map with no Task Router table fails once on the map, and a missing map leaves the Gate unable to run.

files.description: Globs of the documents, against the files git tracks or would track; `*` and `**` skip a name that starts with a dot. Default `docs/**/*.md`.

exempt.description: Globs of the documents left out. Default `docs/research/**`: a research note is read through the spec it backs. A list replaces the default.

markdown-budget.description: Each file a glob of `budgets` matches within that glob's `maxBytes`, and every glob matching a file. A glob matches the files git tracks or would track, a symbolic link left out when the file it points at is matched too; `*` and `**` skip a name that starts with a dot.

budgets.description: Default `docs/agents/*.md` within 6144 bytes; a list replaces the default, such as one that adds `GLOSSARY.md` at a budget of its own.

markdown-refs.description: Every relative link and image in the markdown files resolves: its path to a file or directory git tracks or would track, its heading anchor to a heading of the markdown file it names, and `#anchor` alone to a heading of its own file. A link with a scheme, such as `https:`, and a link inside code are not judged.

files.description: Globs of the markdown files whose links are judged, against the files git tracks or would track; `*` and `**` skip a name that starts with a dot. Default `**/*.md`.

exempt.description: Globs of the files left out. Default none.

temporal-language.description: No changelog phrase in a durable document, matched across a line break and never inside code: `now we`,`we now`, `we no longer`, `previously we`, `as before`, `were removed`, `was` or `were retired`, `no longer` before `support`, `accept`, `require`, `use`, `fan`, `carry`, `replay`, `incur`, `authoritative`, `insert` or `needed`,`is now a` or `the`, `are now`, `previously a` or `the`, `recently` before `changed`, `added`, `updated`, `removed` or `introduced`, and `used to support` or `require`.

files.description: Globs of the durable documents, against the files git tracks or would track; `*` and `**` skip a name that starts with a dot. Default `**/*.md`.

exempt.description: Globs of the files that record a point in time. Default `docs/adr/**`, `docs/decisions/**`, `docs/research/**` and `**/CHANGELOG.md`; a list replaces the default.

decision-records.description: The records of each directory of `dirs` that exists, the files in it git tracks or would track named `<number>-<slug>.md`: numbered from 1 with no gap and no number taken twice, each with a level-1 heading for its title and a frontmatter `status` whose first word is one of `statuses`, so `superseded by ADR 0008` reads as `superseded`. The Gate cannot run when none of `dirs` exists.

dirs.description: The directories of the records, relative to the repository root; one that does not exist holds none. Default `docs/adr` and `docs/decisions`.

fields.description: The frontmatter fields each record is held to beyond `status`; none by default. `date`: every record carries the day it was decided, `YYYY-MM-DD`. `touches`: a record in force, its status `accepted` or `active`, names the paths it governs. Each is a file or directory git tracks or would track, or a glob that matches such a file. A `superseded` record names none. `superseded-by`: a `superseded` record names the number of each record that replaces it. `amended-by`: each number it names is the number of a record. A number names a record in the same directory. A list is comma-separated after its key, or one `- ` item a line under it.

file-size-ratchet.description: The file-size Ratchet, which holds code: each file git tracks or would track within the line limit of its group, or, where `.ai/file-size-ratchet.baseline.json` lists it, within the count recorded there. A file belongs to the first group with a glob that matches it; a file no group matches has no limit, and a symbolic link is left out when the file it points at is matched too. The baseline is committed and lists the files over their limit; one that lists a file twice, at a count within its group's limit or in no group fails the Check. `dw-sdlc gate --update-baseline` records it where there is none and otherwise only tightens it, and only when every Step and every other Check passes: a file within its limit leaves it, a count that shrank is lowered, and no file joins.

groups.description: Default, in this order: `tests`, 2000 lines, a file under a `test`, `tests` or `__tests__` directory or named `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*`; `source`, 500 lines, JavaScript, TypeScript and shell. No default group holds markdown: `agents-map` and `markdown-budget` hold it to byte budgets.

name.description: The group's name, which its failure lines carry: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

files.description: Globs against the path from the repository root, as Node's `path.matchesGlob` reads them: `**` crosses directories, but no `*` matches a name that starts with a dot.

comment-budget.description: The comment budget: each comment block in the JavaScript, TypeScript and shell (`.sh`) files under `roots` carries at most `maxProseLines` lines of prose, a line with a letter or a digit once the comment markers are off. A block is one `/* … */` comment or a run of `//` or `#` comments each alone on consecutive lines; a comment after code on its line is none, and so is a shell `#` that does not start a word of code.

roots.description: The directories whose files it reads, relative to the repository root; one that does not exist holds no file. Default `packages`, `plugins`, `scripts` and `src`.

disable-directives.description: Every Disable directive in a comment gives a reason: `oxlint-disable*` and `eslint-disable*` in every form, `@ts-expect-error` and `@ts-ignore` in JavaScript and TypeScript, `rubocop:disable` in Ruby and `noqa` in Python. A reason is text after `--` on the directive's line; for `@ts-expect-error` and `@ts-ignore`, text after the directive, with or without `:`; or a comment on the line directly above. A directive inside a string or a template is none, and a rule set to `off` in a lint config is not judged. A hard fail, with no Ratchet; the Gate runs it, never a session hook.

files.description: Globs of the files to read, against the files git tracks or would track; `*` and `**` skip a name that starts with a dot. Default every JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby (`.rb`, `.rake`, `.gemspec`, `.ru`, `Rakefile`, `Gemfile`) and Python file.

exempt.description: Globs of the files left out. Default `references/**`, `**/vendor/**` and `**/node_modules/**`; a list replaces the default.

pr.description: How the Ship script, `dw-sdlc pr ship`, ends a pull request. The local override may tighten `merge` and `review` and never loosen them.

merge.description: Who merges a pull request that is green, reviewed and authored by the account `gh` runs as. `auto`: the script squash merges it, naming the head it read. `ask`: it parks with the merge command for the dev. Default `ask`, which an invalid layer runs too. Strictest first: ask, auto.

review.description: The Review depth of a head the Ship script finds unreviewed, which the dev's `--review` overrides for one call. `full`: the agent runs the command `pr.reviewCommand` names over the changes. `light`: one `sdlc-reviewer` subagent reads the diff at medium effort. `off`: the script posts the `dw-sdlc/review` success itself and no one reads them. `auto`: built-in rules route the depth from the changes the Review would read: lockfiles alone `off`; a file under `.github/workflows/`, more than 100 changed lines outside lockfiles, or a change the script cannot size, more files than GitHub's compare lists or a file outside lockfiles with no patch, `full`; the rest `light`. Default `auto`; an invalid layer runs `full`. Strictest first: full, auto, light, off.

reviewCommand.description: The slash command a `full` Review runs over the pull request's changes, as `/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr code errors`. Default `/code-review`. No strictness order: the local override sets it freely.

worker.description: How a Worker's Claude Code session starts: the command, the model and the effort. No strictness order, as with `pr.reviewCommand`: any layer sets any key freely.

command.description: The command a Worker starts with: the words that start its Claude Code session, before the flags of its own, such as `--model` and `--effort`. Default `claude`. It belongs to one machine, so it sits in the local layer, where `dw-sdlc setup` writes `cswap run -- --dangerously-skip-permissions` when `cswap` is on PATH.

model.description: The model a Worker runs on, as Claude Code's `--model` takes it. Default `sonnet`.

effort.description: The effort a Worker runs at, one of Claude Code's effort levels. Default `high`.

setup.description: Commands a fresh linked worktree needs before work starts. Reported at session start, not run.
